ShortDescription.Value: Makes the in-game weather look like the current real weather of any city you choose. Purely cosmetic.

Publish.LongDescription:
# Real Weather Sync
The world is burning. Let your cims burn with you.
## Setup
1. Enable the mod. 2. Type a city, press **Search**, pick yours from the results. 3. Done.
No coordinates, no config files, no weather codes, no manual sliders.
## Two ways to run it
**Live** - the default. Your city gets the chosen city's weather *right now*, refreshed every 15, 30 or 60 minutes.
**Follow the in-game clock** - your city replays that city's **last 24 hours** of real weather, hour by hour, matched to your own clock.
> Say you picked Lyon. It is 10:00 in the real world and 15:00 in your city, so you get the weather Lyon actually had at its most recent 15:00. Your clock rolls on to 16:00, you get its 16:00. A full in-game day replays a full real day.
The weather slides continuously between hours, so nothing ever jumps. And the in-game clock is only *read*, never changed.
## What you get
- **Temperature, clouds, rain and fog** from the real city, fading smoothly between readings. - **Search** shows region, country and coordinates, so you pick the right Springfield. Cities you have used before are one click away. - **Offline-proof** - it holds the last good reading instead of dumping you into a cloudless void. - **Real snow.** The game picks rain or snow from temperature, so the mod nudges it below freezing when the city is genuinely under snow. Optional. - Powered by [Open-Meteo](https://open-meteo.com/): no account, no sign-up, no API key.
## And it actually matters
The mod writes the same four climate values the game's own weather tools write - and the game reads them back. So the weather you choose has consequences:
- **Heating bills** and **building upkeep** follow the temperature - **Fire risk** follows temperature and rain - **Tourism** and **leisure** follow both - **Snow settles** on the ground, **surfaces get wet** - **Weather events** can be influenced - only if you have natural disasters switched on
Solar output and groundwater are never affected, and fog changes nothing but the view.
Want it purely visual? Switch off **Synchronise temperature** in Advanced - that is what most of those systems read.
It still adds no systems, changes no rules, never moves the clock, date or season, and writes **nothing** into your save.
## Options nobody asked for
- **Time shift** - the weather from up to 24 hours into the past, or the future. - **Antipode mode** - the exact opposite side of the planet. For most of Europe, the middle of the South Pacific. - **Take me somewhere awful** - one click to Yakutsk, Ushuaia, Death Valley or Cherrapunji. Also the fastest way to see proper snow. - **Opposite day** - warm becomes cold, clear becomes overcast, dry becomes soaking.
## Before you install
**Do not run this alongside another weather mod** - Time and Weather Anarchy, Weather Plus, Nice Weather, day/night switchers. They will fight over the same values. Real Weather Sync spots the known ones and stands down, but that check works by name, so it is a guard rail rather than a guarantee.
Only the city name you type and the coordinates it resolves to ever leave your PC - no telemetry, no accounts. MIT licence, [source on GitHub](https://github.com/merrinaf-tech/Real-Weather-Sync), weather data by [Open-Meteo](https://open-meteo.com/) under [CC BY 4.0](https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/).
Publish.ChangeLog:
# 1.3.0
## An honest correction
Every version up to now told you this mod "does not touch the simulation". **That was wrong**, and I would rather say so plainly than quietly change the wording.
The mod writes the same four climate values the game's own developer weather tools write. It turns out the game reads those values back, so the weather it sets behaves like real weather:
- **Heating and cooling demand** follows temperature - **Building upkeep** follows temperature - **Fire risk** follows temperature and rain - **Leisure and tourism** follow temperature and rain - **Snow on the ground** and **wet surfaces** follow temperature and precipitation - **Weather events** can be influenced by temperature, rain and cloud cover - and only if you have natural disasters switched on for your city
Verified as **not** affected: solar panel output and groundwater, which always use the game's own weather. Fog changes nothing outside the visuals.
Nothing changed in the code to cause this - it has behaved this way since 1.0.0. What changed is that it is now measured, documented and controllable. The mod still adds no systems, changes no rules and writes nothing into your save.
## New: Synchronise temperature
A switch in the Advanced options, on by default. Turn it off and the mod drives only cloud cover, precipitation and fog, leaving the temperature to the game.
Temperature is what most of those systems read, so this is the single most effective way to keep the mod's influence to a minimum. The cost is that the game can no longer tell rain from snow, and the temperature you see is the game's own. "Show snow when it is really snowing" is disabled while it is off, since that option works by nudging the temperature.
## New: a straight answer inside the mod
The Advanced options now carry a short note explaining exactly what the game reads back, so you do not have to come to this page to find out.
